researched_by: desk research from council's own published pages
policy_summary:
Pilot scheme: three coastal car parks with numbered, bookable motorhome bays for self-contained vehicles, GBP12 per night, 6pm-8am, one night only, online booking only. Overnight sleeping is prohibited in every other council car park, enforced by PCN. A 'motor caravan protocol' was agreed with the AONB. Provision and prohibition published together on the same pages - the clearest published position of any authority researched so far.

The car park pilot is only half the picture. Northumberland County Council also OWNS AND OPERATES A FULL TOURING CAMPSITE - Druridge Bay Campsite, inside its own Druridge Bay Country Park - with 20 hardstanding hookup pitches for caravans and motorhomes, 15 tent pitches, five shower/WC washrooms, a dishwashing kitchen and a waste-water disposal point. It is a straightforward commercial campsite run by the council's parks service, not a parking scheme: GBP32-37 a night in 2026, book online, arrive 2pm, leave by 11am, up to 20 nights. It opened in April 2022 after the council granted itself planning permission, and after a record 2024 season the council extended it through the winter at GBP25 a night rather than closing in October. That is the same authority charging GBP12 for a one-night bay on the coast and GBP32 for a serviced pitch fifteen miles inland - two entirely separate products, published on two entirely separate parts of the website, and only one of them findable from the parking pages.
notes:
IMPORTANT: the restriction is on SLEEPING IN ANY TYPE OF VEHICLE, not on motorhomes specifically. That is the broadest definition encountered - it catches car campers too. The provision, by contrast, requires a self-contained motorhome.

POSTURE: the shape here is 'restrict everywhere by default, sell short stays on the coast, sell long stays inland at the country park'. It is not a clean restrict-coast/provide-inland split, because the three GBP12 aire bays are themselves coastal - at Amble, Bamburgh and Beadnell. What the council actually does is refuse informal overnight sleeping absolutely, across the whole car park estate, and then meter every legitimate alternative it offers. Druridge Bay Campsite is the deepest version of that: the council is not tolerating vans, it is competing with the commercial holiday park sector on the same terms, at broadly the same prices, with its own booking system and its own barrier code. The direction of travel is expansionary - campsite built 2022, winter opening added 2024, aire bays retained - but every step adds a paid, booked, rule-bound product rather than any free or tolerated space.

DEPARTMENTAL SPLIT is why this was nearly missed: the aire bays sit under Parking, the campsite under Parks and Countryside. Nothing on the motorhome parking page links to Druridge Bay Campsite and nothing on the campsite page links to the aire bays. A van user reading only the parking pages would conclude Northumberland offers one night for GBP12 and nothing else.

SURROUNDING PRIVATE SUPPLY (checked and deliberately NOT recorded under this authority - do not re-research): Haggerston Castle is Haven; Sandy Bay at Newbiggin is Parkdean Resorts; Beadnell Bay and Dunstan Hill are both Camping and Caravanning Club sites; Berwick Holiday Park is Haven. None of these are council assets despite sitting on or near the same coast as the council's own bays. Amble Harbour Village, which is council-linked through Advance Northumberland, is a row of retail pods - shops and food, no overnight vehicle provision of any kind. Amble Marina is privately operated and Amble harbour is Warkworth Harbour Commissioners, so there is no council harbour offering vehicle stays.

COUNTRY PARKS CHECKED FOR CAMPING AND FOUND TO HAVE NONE: Bolam Lake, Plessey Woods, Tyne Riverside, Tyne Green (Hexham), Queen Elizabeth II (Ashington), Bedlington, Newbiggin Bay, Blyth and Seaton Sluice foreshore. Druridge Bay and Wansbeck Riverside are the only two country parks in the council's estate with overnight provision on them. Northumberlandia is Banks Group / Land Trust land, not a county park, and has no camping.

sites.notes:
THE CATEGORY THIS FILE WAS MISSING: a council-owned, council-operated touring campsite, not a parking scheme. The terms and conditions say in terms 'the site is managed by Northumberland County Council'. Booking, payment and complaints all run through the council; the campsite has its own council phone line (01670 760968) and mailbox (druridgebaycamping@northumberland.gov.uk).

LAYOUT: hardstanding pitches numbered 1-20 take caravans, campervans and motorhomes, all with electric hook-up; tent pitches are lettered A-O, of which A-G have electric. Trailer tents are hardstanding-only. Roof tents allowed on either.

PRICE (2026 council page): hardstanding caravan/campervan GBP32 weekdays outside school holidays, GBP37 at weekends, school holidays and bank holidays. Tents GBP16-GBP35 depending on party size and hook-up. The GBP32 figure is recorded in price_per_night as the base rate.

SEASON: the council's 2026 page advertises March to October. In November 2024 the council announced the site would stay open through the winter at GBP25 a night after a record season of about 2,000 campers, and park4night and Tripadvisor reviewers report January stays, so winter opening is at least intermittent. Treat March-October as the guaranteed season and winter as bookable-if-advertised. VERIFY which applies for winter 2026-27.

HISTORY: camping was part of the country park when it opened in 1986 but the old area was declared 'no longer fit for purpose'. The council applied to itself for the 20-caravan / 7-tent replacement and it was approved, opening April 2022; the tent side has since grown to 15 lettered pitches. Original consent was for a seven-month season, 1 April to 31 October, which is what makes the winter opening worth watching.

MOTORHOME SERVICE: there is a waste-water disposal point and park4night records black-water disposal, but there is no evidence the council sells service-point-only access to non-residents. Assume you must book a pitch.

No self-containment requirement here, in direct contrast to the coastal aire bays.

sites.notes:
RECORDED AS AMBIGUOUS, NOT AS COUNCIL PROVISION. This site sits at the west end of Wansbeck Riverside Park, which IS a Northumberland County Council country park, and it was unambiguously a council site historically: the council's own Wansbeck country park leaflet still on the northumberland.gov.uk media server says 'camping is restricted to the Wansbeck Riverside Park Camp Site', that 'the caravan and camping site at the west end of the park is open all year and offers touring and static facilities', and gives a 'Caravan Site Warden' contact at a wansbeck.gov.uk address - i.e. Wansbeck District Council, abolished in 2009, whose assets passed to NCC. Today the site trades privately as Wansbeck Riverside Caravan Park, describes itself as 'newly developed, family run', sells static holiday homes, and has a residential bungalow on it that has been marketed on Zoopla.

SO: almost certainly council freehold let on a long lease to a private operator, but I could not find the lease, the disposal, or any council statement confirming it, and the current council page for Wansbeck Riverside Park does not mention the caravan park at all. Ownership is NOT confirmed. Do not present this as council provision to a user until the tenure is established - hence confidence low and status unknown.

PITCH TYPES CONFLICT: Camperbug and VisitNorthumberland both list hardstanding pitches taking motorhomes, campervans, caravans and tents with and without hook-up; Pitchup's 2026 listing shows pods and lodges only and states the site does not accommodate motorhomes or caravans. It is possible the touring side has been closed in favour of statics and glamping. VERIFY by phone (01670 518866) before relying on this as a touring stop.

PRICE: GBP12 per night non-electric grass pitch for two people from Camperbug, with extras (awning GBP7, extra vehicle GBP20). Pitchup quotes from GBP120 for pods. Max 7 consecutive nights, arrive 3pm-8pm, depart by 10am.
sites.geocode_precision: the caravan park at the west end of Wansbeck Riverside Park, on the north bank of the River Wansbeck between Ashington and Sheepwash; Pitchup's site-specific pin
sites.geocode_corroboration: Parks & Gardens UK puts Wansbeck Riverside Park itself at 55.171895 / -1.585489, about 800m east-north-east; the offset is in the right direction for a site described in the council's own leaflet as being at the west end of the park, and both sources agree the postcode area is NE63.

open_questions: Does Druridge Bay Campsite open through winter 2026-27, or has it reverted to the March-October season the council's 2026 page advertises and the original planning consent allowed? The 2024 winter opening at GBP25 may have been a one-off.
Can a motorhome that is not booked onto a pitch use the Druridge Bay waste-water and chemical disposal point, and at what charge? No published answer.

Who holds the freehold of Wansbeck Riverside Caravan Park, and on what terms is it let? The council's own historic leaflet describes it as the district council's camp site; it now trades as a private family-run park. The lease or disposal is not published.
Does Wansbeck Riverside still take touring motorhomes and caravans at all, or is it now pods and statics only? Directory listings contradict each other for 2026.

Is the GBP12 aire price still current, or GBP15? Carried over from the previous session and still unresolved - the campsite pricing was updated for 2026 but the motorhome parking page was not obviously refreshed.

Does the council's country park byelaw framework prohibit overnight parking in the country park DAY car parks (as distinct from the campsite)? The 'additional information' page covers parking charges and permits but says nothing about overnight, so the estate-wide car park sleeping ban is presumed to apply.
price_warning: Sources conflict on price. GBP12 appears throughout 2022-2023 reporting and user reviews; a 2026 listing quotes GBP15 for the overnight permit. Check the council booking system before publishing either figure.
